title: Upload
description:
What the binary sends to a server for one session. Sending the same
session again replaces what the server has: the key is
(`session.machine_id`, `session.source`, `session.session_id`).

schema_version.description: Version of the session record format.

rewrite.description:
Latest rewrite measurement. Null if the session changed no files or
they could not be measured.

lines.description:
The lines the agent added, as hashes, so a server can tell which lines
of a pull request an agent wrote. Sent only when that is switched on
(`sessionly settings --line-hashes on`); empty otherwise.

checkpoints.description:
The rewrite measurement as it was 1, 7 and 30 days after the session
ended, for each of those ages it has reached and was measured at.
Left out while there is none.

source.description: Agent that produced the session, e.g. "claude-code".

collector_version.description: Version of the sessionly binary that built this record.

machine_id.description:
Random id of the sessionly installation that captured the session.
Together with `source` and `session_id` it identifies the record.

captured_by.description: Where the activity (prompts, tool calls, files) was read from.

content.description:
How much content the record carries. Records leave a machine only as
`previews` or `metadata`.

user.description:
Who ran the session: from git config on the machine that captured it,
or, for a session that ran in the cloud, the person the platform says
started it (git there is set up as the agent).

runtime.description: Where the session ran, if not on a person's own machine.

duration_ms.description:
Wall-clock span from first to last activity. Includes idle time and gaps
between resumes, so it can be days for a long-lived session.

active_ms.description: Time the agent spent working on prompts (sum of prompt turn durations).

end_reason.description:
Why the session last ended, as reported by the agent. Null while it is
open, including after it has been resumed.

captured_from_start.description:
False when capture began partway through the session (the hooks were
installed after it started). Prompts, tool calls and files then cover
only the captured part, while cost and usage cover the whole session.

cwd.description: Working directory the session ran in.

entrypoint.description:
How the agent was started, e.g. "cli" or "sdk-cli"; for a cloud
session, what the platform says started it ("remote_mobile", "website").

models.description: Models that answered at least one request, most used first.

permission_modes.description: Permission modes seen during the session, in order of first use.

cost.description: Null when no transcript was available to read cost from.

usage.description: Token usage per model, main thread and subagents combined.

files.description:
Files read or changed through the agent's file tools, and by its shell
commands where the hooks saw them: the working tree is compared before
and after each command. In the cloud everything that changed counts.
On a person's own machine that depends on `--shell-edits`: by default
only what is sure to be the command's, with `all` everything that
changed meanwhile, with `off` nothing.

reviews.description:
Times a review command ran in the session (see `reviews`): the same
in every content mode, since nothing of a run's arguments is kept but
the effort and a pull request number.

instruction_files.description: Instruction files (CLAUDE.md, rules) loaded into the session.

CapturedBy.description: Where a session's activity was read from.

oneOf.description: Hook events, as they happened.
Reconstructed afterwards from the agent's transcript.

Content.description: How much content a record carries.

oneOf.description: As built on the capturing machine: previews and absolute paths. Never uploaded.

Previews kept (the first 200 characters of prompts, shell commands,
search patterns, URLs and error output). Paths are made relative.

No text from prompts, commands or output at all: counts, sizes,
timings, tool names and relative file paths only.

Runtime.description:
A session that a cloud platform ran in a sandbox of its own: a Claude Code
cloud session or a Cursor cloud agent. Such a record's `machine_id` is
"cloud", since the sandbox is new each time.

id.description:
The platform's own id for the session (`cse_…`, `bc-…`), which is
what its web pages and API go by.

oneOf.description: A value written by a newer version.

root.description: Repository root on the capturing machine.

total_usd.description: Best figure for the whole session, in USD.

transcript_estimate_usd.description: Estimate from the token counts visible in the transcript.

unpriced_requests.description:
Requests the total leaves out: made on a model without a known price,
outside any run the agent recorded a total for.

untracked_usd.description:
Spend the agent recorded that the transcript does not show. Null when
it can't be worked out (no recorded total, or a model without a known price).

prompts_covered.description:
How many of the session's prompts the figure covers, when it can't
cover them all: an agent that reports usage only to hooks (Cursor) has
none for turns that ran before the hooks were installed. Null when the
figure covers the whole session.

by_branch.description:
`total_usd` by the branch that was checked out when it was spent,
where the agent says which with every response (Claude Code): a
server then counts for a pull request what was spent on its branch
and on the one it is based on, and not what was spent on others.
Shared out as the estimates of the responses on each branch are; a
branch of null is the responses that named none. Left out where
that is not known, and of a session in the cloud, whose sandbox
holds the one branch.

CostSource.description: Where a session's cost figure comes from.

oneOf.description: The agent's own total, covering every message in the transcript.

The agent's total for one run, combined with our estimates for
messages outside that run.

Our estimate from token counts only. A lower bound: it misses calls
that never reach the transcript.
An estimate that leaves out requests to models without a known price.
A value written by a newer version.

BranchCost.description: What a session spent while one branch was checked out.

cache_write_5m_tokens.description: Cache writes with a 5-minute lifetime (1.25x the input price).

cache_write_1h_tokens.description: Cache writes with a 1-hour lifetime (2x the input price).

estimated_cost_usd.description: Null when the model has no known price.

events.description: Raw hook events the record was built from.

permission_requests.description: Times the user was asked to approve a tool call.

permission_denials.description: Tool calls refused by auto mode.

reviews.description:
Review runs: the length of `Session::reviews`. Left out for an agent
whose review commands are not read (none of the four today): not
known, which is not none.

api_errors.description: Turns that ended in an API error.

ended_at.description:
When the agent finished responding. Null if the turn was interrupted
or is still running.

outcome.description: Null if the turn was interrupted or is still running.

error.description: API error type when outcome is "api_error".

Text.description: A piece of text kept as hash, length and short preview.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the full text, hex.

oneOf.description: A value written by a newer version.

prompt_id.description: Prompt turn the call belongs to.

agent_id.description: Set when a subagent made the call.

skill.description:
For a `Skill` call, the skill's name as written (`code-review`,
`plugin:name`). A name, like the tool's, so it is kept in every
content mode; its arguments are not.

model.description:
Model that made the call. Null where the agent does not say: Grok, and
Cursor turns the hooks did not see.

file_path.description: File the call operated on, for file tools.

input_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the full tool input (JSON), hex.

input_summary.description:
Short human-readable summary of the input: the command, pattern, URL
or description, depending on the tool.

output_bytes.description: Size of the tool's result as serialized JSON.

error.description:
Start of the error message for failed calls. For shell commands this
is the start of the command's output.

oneOf.description: The user interrupted it.
Refused by auto mode or a permission rule.

The user declined the permission prompt. Known only for sessions read
from a transcript; a hook-captured one shows `no_result` instead.

Attempted, but no result was captured: rejected by the user,
interrupted, or still running.
A value written by a newer version.

created.description: True if the agent created the file in this session.

ReviewRun.description:
One run of a review command: `/code-review` and the like (the names are
in `reviews`).

id.description:
The tool-use id of the Skill call; for a slash command, the turn's
prompt id, or one made from its time where there is none.

command.description:
What was run, as written: "code-review", "ultrareview", "review",
"security-review", or a plugin's "name:code-review".

effort.description:
The first argument when it is one of low, medium, high, xhigh, max
or ultra. Else none.

pull_number.description:
A pull request number among the arguments: `621`, `#528` or a pull
request's URL. Else none.

target.description:
What Codex's `/review` was pointed at: `base_branch` (the changes
against a branch), `uncommitted_changes`, `commit` or `custom`. None
for the other agents, whose commands take a pull request.

agent_id.description: Set when a subagent ran it.

duration_ms.description:
From the start to the end of the last of its subagents, or the
call's own duration where it had none.

subagents.description:
Subagents that did the review: the one a skill forks to run in, and
those started from the review's thread before the person's next
prompt, with the subagents they started in turn.

estimated_cost_usd.description:
Those subagents' estimated cost. A floor: the main thread's own
tokens during the review are not in it. Null when none has a cost,
and for a review that ran in the cloud, which is billed apart.

findings.description:
How many findings it reported, where that can be told: from a list
the agent reports (`ReportFindings`, or Codex's own), or else from
the reply that ends the review, where it says how many. Null when
neither says: not known, which is not zero.

oneOf.description: The model called the `Skill` tool.
The person typed the command.
Codex's `/review`.
A value written by a newer version.
On the machine (or sandbox) the session ran in.
In the cloud: `/ultrareview`, `/code-review ultra`.
A value written by a newer version.

RewriteMeasurement.description: How much of a session's changes is still in the files, measured later.

branch.description: Branch and commit that were checked out when measuring.

files_rewritten.description: Files where less than half of the agent's lines survive, or that are gone.

lines_added.description: Lines the agent added that are tracked (not blank or punctuation-only).

lines_surviving.description: How many of them are still in the files.

AddedLines.description:
Lines an agent added to one file with one model. A line is hashed without
the whitespace at its ends; blank lines and lines without a letter or
digit are left out. The same line added twice is listed twice.

model.description: Null if the model is not known.

hashes.description: First 8 bytes of each line's SHA-256, as 16 hex digits.

RewriteCheckpoint.description:
How much of a session's changes was still in the files at a fixed age
after it ended: the first measurement taken at or after that age. Counts
and times only. Once taken it is kept as it is.

checkpoint.description: The age it is for: `1d`, `7d` or `30d` after the session ended.

added.description: Lines the agent added that are tracked, when this was measured.

surviving.description: How many of them were in the files then.

age_seconds.description:
How long after the session ended it was measured, which is the age
or more: a machine that was off on the day measures later.

ended_at.description:
When the session had ended, as that age was counted. A checkpoint
belongs to this end: of a session that has another end now (it went
on since), it is a checkpoint no more.
